requests_made.purpose: retrieve the public agenda listing, whose HTML body embeds a genuine <script type="application/ld+json"> Event array directly (no HTML-card scraping needed)
requests_made.retained_fixture: fixtures/lav/agenda-excerpt.html (the full, unmodified 10-event JSON-LD block plus a minimal wrapper — every field retained verbatim)

requests_made.purpose: venue-identity research only (not an Observation acquisition request) — corroborates the address already found in the agenda page's own JSON-LD

findings.pagination: Not investigated — 10 upcoming events were returned by a single fetch; no next-page indicator was present.
findings.stable_identifier: No numeric id is exposed in the JSON-LD; every Event's own permalink slug (from its own `url` field, /evento/{slug}/) is used as source_record_id.
findings.date_time: startDate/endDate carry an explicit '+00:00' UTC offset — a genuinely confirmed UTC instant (unlike Super Bock Arena's own Events-Calendar list view, which carries no offset at all). certainty is honestly UTC_INSTANT.
findings.music_filtering: No per-event category/genre field exists anywhere in this source's JSON-LD. Every retained record becomes an Observation, matching the existing MEO Arena/Village Underground precedent for a single music/nightlife VENUE-type source with no per-event taxonomy to filter on.
findings.venue_identity: Most records' location.name is the bare string 'LAV'; two records ('LAV – Sala 1', 'LAV – Sala 2') additionally carry a fully-populated location.address PostalAddress — this venue's own first-party address evidence, used to admit it as a new ADDRESS_ONLY canonical Venue via `npm run onboard:venues` (never hand-authored). Room-level location.name is retained in source_fields.room only, matching the Casa da Música 'room is not a separate venue' precedent.
